chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muʿammar ibn Khallād, he said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: Is it sufficient for a man to wipe his feet with the leftover moisture of his head? He indicated with his head: No. I said: With new water? He indicated with his head: Yes.
And the report that al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Shuʿayb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wiping the head. I said: Should I wipe my head with the dampness that is in my hand? He said: “No. Rather, you place your hand in the water and then wipe.”

So these reports were issued out of taqiyyah and in accordance with the doctrine of the opponents. What indicates that is what we have mentioned previously of the reports containing the negation of taking water for wiping, and contradiction is not permissible in their sayings and actions. It is also possible that what was meant by it is when his face or the limbs of his taharah have dried, so that he needs to renew his washing, and thus he takes new water, and that taking would be for wiping according to what the report contains. It is also possible that by the second report, in his statement, “Rather, you place your hand in the water,” he meant the water that remained in his beard or eyebrows; and there is nothing in the report stating that he places his hand in the water that is in the vessel or elsewhere. If that possibility is admitted, the contradiction among them is nullified. And what indicates this interpretation is:

key_terms.النَّدَى: dampness or moisture remaining on the hand
key_terms.بِمَاءٍ جَدِيدٍ: with new water, meaning freshly taken water for wiping
key_terms.طَهَارَتِهِ: his state or acts of ritual purity
key_terms.قَدَمَيْهِ: his two feet, the limbs being wiped in the report
key_terms.لِلتَّقِيَّةِ: for taqiyyah, dissimulation under circumstances requiring caution
key_terms.مَسْحِ الرَّأْسِ: wiping the head as part of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يَمْسَحَ: to wipe in the ritual act of masḥ during wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Can fresh water be used for wiping the head and feet in wudu according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage discusses legal reports concerning wiping in wudu (ablution), especially whether fresh water may be taken for wiping the head or feet. The compiler explains that such reports are either to be understood as taqiyyah or interpreted in a way that removes contradiction with other narrations that prohibit taking new water for masḥ.
